config.title: gap in Flex and Grid

intro.title: gap in Flex and Grid
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage layout to practice using the 'gap' property in CSS. You'll learn how to add consistent spacing between items in both Flexbox and Grid containers without using margins. The core concept is understanding how 'gap' creates visual separation and improves layout control. You'll work with CSS properties like 'display: flex', 'display: grid', and the 'gap' property itself. By the end, you'll be able to create cleaner, more maintainable layouts with evenly spaced elements.
intro.usecase: The `gap` property is essential for creating clean, consistent spacing in modern UI layouts without relying on margins or padding on individual items. You'll use it in product dashboards to evenly space metric cards, in navigation menus to separate links, and in filter panels to align checkboxes or chips. This approach simplifies responsive design for galleries, forms, and data tables, ensuring elements maintain proportional breathing room across screen sizes.

objectives: Apply the gap property to create consistent spacing between flex items
Configure gap values to control spacing in both rows and columns of a grid layout
Implement gap shorthand syntax to set row and column spacing simultaneously
Manipulate gap spacing to adjust visual hierarchy in flex and grid containers
Construct responsive layouts by adjusting gap values with media queries
Integrate gap with other flex and grid properties to create cohesive layouts
Initialize gap spacing in both flex and grid containers to replace margin-based spacing

steps.title: Create a container with flex display
steps.instruction: Create a CSS class named .flex-container that sets display to flex to establish a flex layout context.
steps.hint: Start by writing a CSS rule that targets the .flex-container class and sets the display property to flex.
steps.expectedOutcome: A .flex-container class is created with display: flex; to serve as the foundation for a flex layout.
successCriteria: The .flex-container class exists and has display: flex; property set.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the .flex-container class, but it's missing the display: flex; property. Add display: flex; to make it a proper flex container.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .flex-container class isn't properly defined. Make sure you create a CSS rule for .flex-container with display: flex;.

steps.title: Add child elements to the flex container
steps.instruction: Create a CSS class named .flex-item with background color #3498db, padding 20px, and margin 4px.
steps.hint: Define the .flex-item class in your CSS file, then create multiple div elements in your HTML with class='flex-item'.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a .flex-item class defined with styling, and 4-6 div elements with this class in your HTML to serve as flex items.
successCriteria: The .flex-item class is defined with background-color, padding, and margin properties, and there are 4-6 div elements with class='flex-item' in the HTML.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've made progress, but make sure you have both the CSS class definition and the HTML elements. Check that your .flex-item class has all three properties (background-color, padding, margin) and you have 4-6 div elements.
steps.feedbackWrong: The flex items aren't properly set up. You need to define a .flex-item CSS class with the specified styling and create multiple div elements with that class in your HTML.

steps.title: add 4-6 div elements with this class inside t
steps.instruction: add 4-6 div elements with this class inside the flex container in your HTML.
steps.hint: Define the .flex-item class in your CSS file, then create multiple div elements in your HTML with class='flex-item'.
steps.feedbackPartial: Review the instruction and try again.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the instruction and try again.

steps.title: Apply gap property to flex container
steps.instruction: Inside the .flex-container class, add the CSS property gap: 20px; to create equal spacing between all flex items.
steps.hint: The gap property controls the spacing between flex items. Add it after the display property in your .flex-container selector.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .flex-container class will have a gap property that creates 20px spacing between all flex items.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added gap: 20px; inside the .flex-container selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: The gap property wasn't added correctly. Check that you've added gap: 20px; to the .flex-container class.

steps.title: Create a grid container
steps.instruction: Create a new CSS class named .grid-container with display: grid; and grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); to set up a 3-column grid layout.
steps.hint: Add a new CSS rule below your existing flex container. Use the selector .grid-container and set the display property to grid, then define the columns.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new .grid-container CSS class will be created with grid display and a 3-column layout.
successCriteria: The .grid-container class exists with display: grid; and grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the .grid-container class, but it's missing either the display: grid; or grid-template-columns property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .grid-container class is missing or doesn't have the correct properties. Make sure to include both display: grid; and grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);

steps.title: Add child elements to the grid container
steps.instruction: Create a CSS class named .grid-item with the same styling as the .flex-item class (width, height, background-color, border). Then, in your HTML, add 6-9 div elements with the class 'grid-item' inside the grid container.
steps.hint: Copy the .flex-item styling to create .grid-item. In your HTML, add multiple div elements with class='grid-item' between the grid container's opening and closing tags.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a .grid-item class defined with the same styling as .flex-item, and 6-9 grid items added to the grid container in your HTML.
successCriteria: The .grid-item class is defined with width, height, background-color, and border properties, and 6-9 div elements with class='grid-item' are present inside the grid container in the HTML.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've both defined the .grid-item class with the required styling AND added 6-9 div elements with that class inside the grid container in your HTML.
steps.feedbackWrong: The grid items aren't properly set up. Remember to create a .grid-item CSS class with the same styling as .flex-item, then add 6-9 div elements with that class inside the grid container in your HTML.

steps.title: Apply gap property to grid container
steps.instruction: Add the CSS property gap: 15px; to the existing .grid-container class to create spacing between grid items in both rows and columns.
steps.hint: The gap property works the same way in grid containers as it does in flex containers. Add it inside the .grid-container rule.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .grid-container class will have a gap property that creates 15px spacing between all grid items.
successCriteria: The .grid-container class contains the property gap: 15px;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added gap: 15px; exactly as specified inside the .grid-container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The gap property hasn't been added correctly to the .grid-container class. Check that you've written gap: 15px; inside the .grid-container rule.

steps.title: Experiment with different gap values in flex
steps.instruction: In the .flex-container class, change the gap property value from 10px to 2rem to see how different units affect the spacing between flex items.
steps.expectedOutcome: The flex container's gap property will be updated to use rem units, demonstrating how different CSS units affect spacing.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've changed the gap value to exactly '2rem' in the .flex-container class.
steps.feedbackWrong: The gap property in .flex-container should be updated to 'gap: 2rem;' to complete this step.

steps.title: Experiment with different gap values in grid
steps.instruction: In the .grid-container class, change the gap value from 15px to 25px.
steps.hint: Look for the comment '/* Add gap: 15px; here */' in the .grid-container class and replace it with 'gap: 25px;'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The grid container will have a gap of 25px between rows and columns.
successCriteria: The .grid-container class has 'gap: 25px;' instead of the comment placeholder.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've replaced the comment with 'gap: 25px;' exactly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The gap value in .grid-container should be 25px. Look for the comment in that class and replace it with the correct property.

steps.title: Use row-gap and column-gap separately in grid
steps.instruction: In the .grid-container class, replace the single gap property with row-gap: 20px; and column-gap: 30px; to create different spacing for rows and columns.
steps.hint: Remove the comment placeholder and add the two separate properties instead of the single gap property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The grid container will have 20px spacing between rows and 30px spacing between columns, demonstrating independent control of row and column gaps.
successCriteria: The .grid-container class contains row-gap: 20px; and column-gap: 30px; properties (not the single gap property).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've replaced the single gap property with both row-gap and column-gap properties with the specified values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .grid-container class should have row-gap: 20px; and column-gap: 30px; instead of the single gap property.

steps.title: Use row-gap and column-gap separately in flex
steps.instruction: In the .flex-container class, replace the single gap property with separate row-gap and column-gap properties to see how they affect flex layouts.
steps.hint: Replace 'gap: 10px;' with 'row-gap: 15px;' and 'column-gap: 25px;' in the .flex-container class.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .flex-container class will have separate row-gap and column-gap properties instead of a single gap property.
successCriteria: The .flex-container class contains both row-gap: 15px; and column-gap: 25px; properties, and the original gap property is removed.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've removed the original 'gap: 10px;' property and added both 'row-gap: 15px;' and 'column-gap: 25px;' to the .flex-container class.
steps.feedbackWrong: In the .flex-container class, replace 'gap: 10px;' with 'row-gap: 15px;' and 'column-gap: 25px;' to use separate gap properties.
